# Icon

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

In a Server Component, which is almost everywhere. The icon data is loaded on the server,
so the browser downloads one inline `<svg>` and no icon library.

```tsx
<Icon name="check" size="md" />
<Icon name="arrow-right" label="Next page" />
```

Leave `label` unset for decoration - the icon is then hidden from screen readers. In a
Client Component use `<Svg icon={check} />` instead, which takes the same props.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Icon } from 'topclassui/icon'
```

## Props

Required: `name`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | **yes** | `IconName` | - | One of the 84 built-in icon names, loaded on the server. |
| `flipRtl` | no | `boolean` | - | Defaults to true for directional icons (arrows, carets). |
| `label` | no | `string` | - | Set for a meaningful icon; leave unset or empty for a decorative one. |
| `size` | no | `IconSize \| number \| (string & {})` | - | The five names, or any CSS length. Defaults to 1em so the icon follows the text. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
